correctness.rationale: The theorem fixes all quantifiers (every finite n>=1, omega>0, random complex Haar pure vector and fixed product-basis dephasing). Uniform-simplex affine coordinates prove exact rank expectations. Binomial CLT plus second-moment convergence gives L2 quantile convergence and harmonic dominance yields L2 weight convergence; Gaussian integration by parts recovers the coefficient. CPTP trace contraction and the ergotropy trace-norm bound yield conservative 4n omega Haar-sphere Lipschitz constant and the explicit Levy tail. The ratio follows from the separately concentrated energy. Exact rational n<=8, combinatorial labels and 48000 separately generated Dirichlet samples check normalizations; none is substituted for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Statement-by-statement comparisons isolate a different, previously uncomputed idealized ensemble: a Haar-pure state after full fixed-product-basis dephasing with binomial spin energies. The 2025 primary paper contains the general rearrangement but uses different random sampling and no exact Dirichlet(1) harmonic/spin law; the 2024 paper proves the generic concentration method only, which is credited and not asserted novel; the 2020 paper studies fixed-unitary work. The 2026 motivation concerns a driven interacting battery, with only abstract accessible and a material residual priority risk. Targeted published-source exact-term, alias and equivalent-form searches found no covering result, but searches cannot establish absolute novelty.
residual_risks: The motivating 2026 study full text was not accessible; the publicly readable abstract alone cannot exclude additional appendix results.
Unindexed or inaccessible earlier mathematical statistics/quantum thermodynamics work may already combine Dirichlet(1) order statistics and spin-binomial energies.
The result is a model-independent Haar benchmark; it must not be read as describing the actual Floquet dynamics or every dephasing channel.

value.rationale: A natural quantum-battery storage question asks how much globally extractable work remains after dephasing a chaotic-state benchmark. The answer is not simply no work or all work: it is a sharp residual sqrt(n) energy scale with a non-elementary Gaussian-quantile constant, an exact rational finite-size formula, and a vanishing work/energy fraction. This supplies a transparent benchmark against qualitative high-disorder claims, without asserting a Floquet prediction; model limitations explicitly stated.
